# Correspondence with a Public Body

## When to use this

Use this for any letter written in the Kingdom's name to a mayor, a council
member, a state legislator, a state agency commissioner, a federal agency
official, or the staff who actually handle the file — a town clerk, an assessor,
a zoning enforcement officer, a building official, a records officer. It is the
working form of the protocol in `04-GOVERNMENT-RELATIONS-PROTOCOL`, and that
document should be read once before the first letter goes out.

Do not use it for a public records request, which has its own form and its own
statutory clocks (`connecticut-foia-request`). Do not use it to assert a right
against a private party; that is a demand letter and belongs in a different
register.

The letter is one page. It has five moves and no sixth. Almost every failure in
this field is a failure of posture rather than of drafting — the wrong reader,
the wrong ask, or an opening paragraph that tells the recipient to stop reading.

## Before you send

- [ ] **The right reader has been identified** — the office with authority to
      grant the specific thing wanted, and the named individual within it who
      handles the file. Not the most senior name available. A letter to a mayor
      about a certificate of occupancy is answered, if at all, by the clerk it is
      forwarded to, three weeks later.
- [ ] **The posture is chosen and honest** — petitioner, party, or peer (see the
      Notes below and § 1 of the protocol). Write in the posture the recipient
      will recognise, not the one the Charter assigns.
- [ ] **The name and title are verified this week** from the body's own website
      or a telephone call. Officials move. A letter to a predecessor is read as
      evidence that the sender does not follow the body's affairs.
- [ ] **The specific request appears in the first or second paragraph,** and it
      is something this recipient can actually give.
- [ ] **The authority is cited by section** — the statute, regulation, ordinance,
      or programme criterion relied on. A request grounded in a citation must be
      handled. A request grounded in fairness can be deferred forever.
- [ ] **Nothing in the letter asserts immunity, disclaims the recipient's
      jurisdiction, reserves rights under the Uniform Commercial Code, appears
      "without prejudice", or demands recognition of the Kingdom's status.** Any
      one of these ends the correspondence. See the Notes.
- [ ] **The General Assembly Citation, if mentioned, is described as what it
      is** — a ceremonial honour recognising contribution to cultural heritage,
      civic education, and community empowerment. Never as recognition of tribal
      status, legal status, or a government-to-government relationship.
- [ ] **The signature block carries a name, an office, and a return address,**
      and claims no governmental, judicial, or law-enforcement authority.
- [ ] **The letterhead is plain** — no seal larger than the text, no device
      resembling a badge or a coat of arms of a government, no office name
      imitating a public agency.
- [ ] **The letter is one page,** with anything longer attached rather than
      embedded.
- [ ] **The follow-up date is in the calendar** before the letter is sent, and an
      officer is assigned to make the call.
- [ ] **A record is open in the Government-to-Government Contact Register,** and
      the letter carries its reference. The record is completed the same day the
      letter goes out, not when a reply arrives.
- [ ] **Delivery produces proof** — email with a read receipt where available,
      and for consequential matters certified mail as well.

## The letterhead

```
APEX KINGDOM
[OFFICE OF THE FOUNDER AND PRESIDING OFFICER]
[STREET ADDRESS]
Bridgeport, Connecticut [ZIP]
Telephone [NUMBER] · [EMAIL ADDRESS]
```

## The letter

```
[APEX KINGDOM LETTERHEAD]

[DATE]

BY EMAIL TO [ADDRESS] AND BY CERTIFIED MAIL

[ADDRESS BLOCK IN THE FORM ABOVE]

Re:  [THE SPECIFIC MATTER — e.g., "Application for certificate of
     occupancy, 000 Main Street (Application No. 2026-0000)"]
     Our reference: [G2G RECORD NUMBER]

Dear [SALUTATION IN THE FORM ABOVE]:

I write on behalf of Apex Kingdom, a religious society and charitable
trust affiliated with [CONGREGATION], operating in [BRIDGEPORT] and
serving [DESCRIBE THE COMMUNITY IN A CLAUSE]. [WHERE THE RECIPIENT IS AN
ELECTED OFFICIAL REPRESENTING THE AREA: Our members live and worship in
your [district / ward].]

I am writing to ask that [THE SPECIFIC REQUEST, IN ONE SENTENCE — e.g.,
"your office confirm whether the application referenced above is complete,
and identify the staff member to whom it has been assigned"].

[ONE SHORT PARAGRAPH OF FACTS, ONLY WHAT THE RECIPIENT NEEDS TO ACT.
DATES, FILE NUMBERS, ADDRESSES. NO HISTORY OF THE KINGDOM, NO GRIEVANCE,
NO ARGUMENT NOT REQUIRED BY THE REQUEST.]

The request is made under [CITE THE AUTHORITY BY SECTION — e.g., "Conn.
Gen. Stat. § 12-81(13) and the filing procedure in §§ 12-87 and 12-87a"
— CHECK WITH THE ASSESSOR WHICH SUBDIVISION OF § 12-81 APPLIES TO THIS
PARCEL BEFORE CITING ONE /
"§ [NUMBER] of the [CITY] Zoning Regulations" / "36 C.F.R. § 800.3(f)(3),
under which an agency official may recognise as a consulting party an
organisation with a demonstrated interest in an undertaking"]. [ONE
SENTENCE APPLYING THAT AUTHORITY TO THESE FACTS.]

[WHERE A MEETING IS THE ASK: I would welcome thirty minutes with you or
with the appropriate member of your staff at your convenience, at your
offices or by telephone.]

[WHERE THE CITATION IS GENUINELY RELEVANT AND ONLY THEN: On 5 October 2025
the Connecticut General Assembly issued Apex Kingdom an Official Citation,
introduced by nine legislators of the Bridgeport delegation, recognising
the organisation for advancing cultural heritage, civic education, and
community empowerment. A copy is enclosed for your information.]

If I have not heard from your office by [DATE APPROXIMATELY THREE WEEKS
OUT], I will telephone to follow up. If this matter belongs with another
office, I would be grateful if you would tell me which, and I will write
to them directly.

Thank you for your time and for the work your office does.

Respectfully,

______________________________
[FULL NAME]
[OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
[STREET ADDRESS] · [TELEPHONE] · [EMAIL]

Enclosures:  [LIST, OR OMIT THE LINE]
cc:          [NAME, TITLE — ONLY WHERE THERE IS A REASON]
```

## Notes

**Posture is the whole decision, and it is made before the first word.** The
protocol names three, and choosing the wrong one is the commonest and most
expensive error in this field.

*Petitioner.* The Kingdom asks a body holding authority to grant something — a
permit, an exemption, a grant, admission as a consulting party. This is nearly
every useful interaction with a government. It is not a humiliation. A cathedral
applies for a building permit; a diocese files for tax exemption on the assessor's
form like everyone else. Deference in form costs nothing and buys the reader's
attention. What matters is that the request is precise and well founded.

*Party.* The Kingdom holds procedural rights in a live proceeding — an appeal to a
zoning board of appeals or a board of assessment appeals, a complaint before the
Freedom of Information Commission, a Section 106 consultation. The register here
is technical rather than deferential: know the rule, meet the deadline, build the
record. Parties in these forums lose on procedure far more often than on merits,
and the letter's job is to preserve a point, not to persuade.

*Peer.* Institution to institution. This posture exists only where the
counterparty agrees to it, and nothing the Kingdom writes creates that agreement.
It is genuinely available with congregations, charities, historical societies,
universities, and occasionally a municipality willing to sign a memorandum about
a specific project. It is not available with a state or federal agency as of
right, and writing as a peer to an official who sees a petitioner does not
elevate the Kingdom — it removes the letter from the queue.

One question settles the choice before drafting: *what does this person have the
power to give, and under what authority?*

**Why an assertion of immunity guarantees no reply.** A private association has
no sovereign immunity. Sovereign immunity in the United States belongs to the
federal government, the states, foreign states under the Foreign Sovereign
Immunities Act, and federally recognised Indian tribes; it is not something an
entity confers on itself in its own founding document. So the assertion is not
merely unpersuasive — it is wrong, and the recipient's law department knows it is
wrong. That is the practical mechanism. Public officials meet the vocabulary of
immunity, special appearance, reservation of rights, and non-submission to
jurisdiction constantly, from a population of correspondents whose letters are
routed to counsel and never answered on the merits. The moment that vocabulary
appears, the Kingdom is sorted into that population, and the sorting is
irreversible with that office. Nothing in the letter after the assertion is read.

The same paragraph would have been read with interest had it simply said what the
Kingdom wanted and cited the ordinance.

**Why a demand for recognition guarantees no reply either.** No official at any
level of a state or federal government has authority to recognise a tribe by
letter, and every one of them knows it. A demand for recognition is therefore a
request the recipient cannot grant, attached to a request they could have granted,
and the file goes to the attorney whose function is to say no to the first — who
then says no to both, because that is the safe answer and because the bundle now
looks like the opening move in a dispute rather than an application.

If the Kingdom needs a certificate of occupancy, the letter is about the
certificate of occupancy. Recognition, in the forms actually available — a seat
as a consulting party, a grant awarded, an exemption allowed, a commissioner who
takes the meeting — is built out of a file of granted requests. Each one is a
federal or state document naming the Kingdom, and they compound. The demand
version produces nothing and forecloses the incremental version.

**The signature block, and a word on titles.** Within the Kingdom the Founder is
properly styled the Sovereign, and internal instruments should say so. On a letter
to a city planner, "[Name], Founder and Presiding Officer, Apex Kingdom" is read
and answered; a signature claiming a royal, governmental, or judicial title is
circulated around the office and answered, if at all, by counsel. This is not
timidity. It is the recognition that the letter's job is to be acted on by a
person who has never heard of the Kingdom and who has forty other files.

Two related cautions. Do not sign correspondence to a public body as "Apex
Tactical Corporation" unless that name is in fact an incorporated entity or a
recorded trade name — a name asserting a corporate form the Kingdom does not hold
is exactly the small inaccuracy a municipal attorney notices and keeps. And no
officer signing such a letter may use a title, credential, or device suggesting
peace-officer authority; holding a private officer out as a peace officer is
criminal impersonation under Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 53a-130 and 53a-130a, and one
incident ends the municipal relationship permanently and personally.

**The date at the end is the most useful sentence in the letter.** It is not a
deadline imposed on the recipient — deadlines directed at public officials read as
hostile and are ignored — but a statement of what the Kingdom will do. "If I have
not heard from your office by 14 September, I will telephone" converts silence
from an insult into a scheduled event, gives the recipient a reason to route the
letter before that date, and creates a dated record of diligence that costs
nothing. Then make the call. A follow-up date that passes without a call teaches
the office, correctly, that the Kingdom's dates mean nothing.

**Confirm every commitment in writing within a business day.** Where an official
says on a call or in a meeting that they will do something, send one short
paragraph confirming what was said, attaching nothing, and close with the sentence
that does the work: *if I have misunderstood anything, please tell me and I will
correct my record.* That sentence is polite, genuinely offered, and shifts the
burden. If no correction comes, the Kingdom holds an uncontradicted
contemporaneous account of what a public official undertook to do, which is in
practice the only form in which such an undertaking exists. Officials move,
retire, and forget.

**On RLUIPA, and when not to name it.** The Religious Land Use and
Institutionalized Persons Act, 42 U.S.C. § 2000cc, is the strongest statute the
Kingdom is likely to use, and its power lies in the record rather than in the
threat. Municipal counsel know the statute and advise around it. What they cannot
advise around is a file showing that the applicant stated the religious character
of the use in writing at the outset, applied correctly, identified the secular
assembly uses permitted in the same zone, and received denials whose stated
reasons do not survive that comparison. Build the file in every application. Do
not name the statute in the first letter: invoking it early converts a staff-level
problem into a litigation posture, and the city stops talking and starts
documenting.

**What this letter is never.** It is a request or a statement of position from a
private religious society to a public body. It is not process. It carries no
seal implying judicial authority, no case caption, no docket style, no ordering
language, no notice of default, and no consequence said to follow automatically
from the recipient's silence. That line is set out in `01-LEGAL-POSTURE` § 4 and
it does not move.

*This is an operating template prepared to organise the Kingdom's affairs. It is
not legal advice and no attorney-client relationship arises from it. Forms of
address, office holders, and filing procedures change, and several matters
touched here carry deadlines that cannot be reopened. Engage licensed Connecticut
counsel before acting on any of it.*
